items.text: The current El Niño episode, often described as a "super El Niño," raises concerns about the potential impact of this phenomenon on global temperatures and related health impacts. A new study by the Barcelona Institute for Global Health (ISGlobal) has examined the relationship between this climate phenomenon and temperature-related mortality worldwide. The study, published in Nature Medicine, estimates that very strong El Niño episodes are associated with 107,035 additional heat-related deaths and 112,681 fewer cold-related deaths per year compared with neutral conditions.

items.title: AI analysis of ECG data measured by smartwatch may help detect reduced heart pumping function
items.text: Artificial intelligence (AI) software tasked with evaluating heart signals (ECG data) measured by smartwatches may help identify a hidden and dangerous heart condition known as left ventricular systolic dysfunction (LVSD), although results varied between smartwatch brands and across ECG recordings, according to new, preliminary, independent late-breaking science presented today at the American Heart Association's Scientific Sessions 2026. The meeting takes place Nov. 6–9 in Chicago.

items.title: Chemotherapy for breast cancer linked to accelerated biological aging
items.text: Chemotherapy helps many women survive breast cancer, but new research suggests that chemotherapy may also accelerate biological aging beyond chronological age and increase the risk of earlier death from other causes. The findings point to a need to explore whether interventions to slow or reverse biological aging could improve long-term health for breast cancer survivors.
